title: HCI test case file
description: A list of RAG test cases. Retrieval checks run in pytest; answer checks run in `hci eval` (needs an LLM). Chunk ids are explicit file references, relative to the repo root: `data/paths.json#<scenario>/<location>` (path step), `data/documents/<file>#<n>` (n-th chunk of a document, from 1; positional, so editing the document renumbers later chunks: re-check cases citing it), `data/corrections/<file>.md` (one chunk per correction), `data/explanations/<file>.json#<index>` (example explanation, from 0), and `fact-<n>` for the case's own facts (the facts file is runtime state outside git). pytest checks that every id names an existing file of the repo (never a git-ignored upload) and a chunk produced by `corpus.load()`.

facts.description: Operator updates recorded before the question. They get ids fact-0, fact-1, ... in order.

retrieved.description: Chunk ids that must be in the context.

not_retrieved.description: Chunk ids that must not be in the context.

first.description: Chunk ids that must open the context, in this order.

answer_contains.description: Case-insensitive strings the LLM answer must all contain (hci eval only).

answer_contains_any.description: Case-insensitive strings of which the LLM answer must contain at least one (hci eval only). Defaults to the refusal markers (`REFUSAL_MARKERS` in hci/constants.py) for an unanswerable case.

answer_excludes.description: Case-insensitive strings the LLM answer must not contain (hci eval only). Only strings that prove the model answered, never words a correct refusal restates.

unanswerable.description: The records do not answer the question. With the Jev judge on (hci eval --jev), retrieval passes iff Jev refuses (no context) and `retrieved`/`not_retrieved`/`first` are skipped; with it off (pytest, plain hci eval) they apply as usual. The answer must refuse: it contains one of `answer_contains_any`, by default the refusal markers.

xfail.description: Known failure: the reason. The case still runs and is reported.
